notes: The library list now shows each clip's file size. This explains why one language version of a creative weighs more than another: a body that already matches the render parameters is joined by STREAM COPY, untouched, so its own bitrate carries straight into the final video, while a body that doesn't match gets re-encoded to 8 Mbps. Bigger usually means better here, not worse. Fix (important): the shared library folder accepted a drive.google.com LINK. Nothing can read a URL, and the app then created a folder literally named after it — so the field showed a green ✓ while the library stayed permanently empty (and team presets were being written into that dead folder). Now a link is refused with an explanation, a stored link is ignored on startup, and Settings lists the synced cloud folders it finds on this Mac so you can pick the real path in one click. TRIM is now frame-exact. It used to be stored at 0.1s — three frames at 30fps — so hitting a specific frame was impossible; now every in/out lands on a whole frame of the SOURCE clip's real fps (24 / 25 / 30 / 60, probed per clip), and the label shows both the exact seconds and the frame number. New controls under the bar: '⇤ In = кадр' / 'Out = кадр ⇥' stamp the playhead you parked with ⟨ ⟩ into the trim (keys I and O), ⟨ ⟩ next to each handle nudge it by one frame (Alt + ← / → does the armed handle, Shift for 10), and '▶ стик' / '▶ хвіст' play 1.5s from In / up to Out so you can check the join. Grabbing or nudging a handle now jumps the picture to exactly that frame. Detected scene cuts are drawn on the trim bar and the handles magnet-snap to them within 4 frames — a body part usually starts exactly on a cut. New '⧉ на всі' next to reset: apply this trim to every clip of the pack (localizations are time-aligned to the original, so one cut covers all language versions). And Normalize now applies the trim: press it on a trimmed clip and you get the cut, conformed body ready for the board or the library — before, trim was only applied during the final assemble. Speed + quality: a freshly captioned hook now comes out of the bake with concat-ready AUDIO (44.1 kHz stereo AAC) as well as video. Before, the audio kept the source's rate/channels — so a 48 kHz or mono hook (most phone and AI-generated footage) failed the stream-copy check and got a SECOND full encode before joining: slower and one extra encoding generation on every hook. Fix: 'Merge hooks → one clip' now burns in the TITLES too (captions, trim and stickers already worked). Titles are baked like stickers — always, regardless of the 'Bake captions' switch — and the engine now does a pixel pass for a clip that has only a title and no captions, which is what silently dropped them before. Board: TIME now goes to the RIGHT. Body parts lay out in a row (Body 1 ▸ Body 2 ▸ …) instead of stacking downwards, the board widens as you add parts, and the column is labelled 'час →' — the vertical axis is only the list of creatives, as it always was. Fix: the operation timer showed nonsense ("6h 1m" for 20 seconds) and flickered — two different time formatters shared one name, so milliseconds were being read as seconds. Fix: Trim now sticks to the CLIP — set it, go to another video in the pack, come back, and your in/out is still there (it also travels to the board with the clip). Fix: a hook sent to Body with the ▸ arrow now renders WITH its captions, titles, trim and stickers — before it went in as raw video, because a reused hook was passed as a bare clip reference. Fix (batch): switching between clips in a pack no longer shows the PREVIOUS clip's captions — the layout is now tied to the clip it was built for and refreshes the moment you click another one (no more nudging a caption to wake it up). Titles are now PER CLIP: every video in a pack keeps its own titles (the strip marks a clip with a green 'T'), a new '⧉ Titles → всі кліпи паку' button copies the open clip's titles onto the whole pack, and the panel says whose titles you're editing. Titles localization is finally visible: the LOC tab lists every clip that has titles and gives you an input per language (EN + the languages you ticked) — the copy lives on the clip, so each language version renders its own line; a localized clip opened with ✎ shows and edits ITS language's title text. Titles can now be DRAGGED on the preview (like the stickers in Sub_): grab a title and move it freely in both axes — the cursor turns into a move handle over it, and the Horizontal/Vertical sliders follow live. A new 'Horizontal' slider does the same by hand. The render places the title exactly where you dropped it. Titles: new 'Tilt °' slider (like the sticker overlays) — the title rotates around its own centre, so it stays where you placed it, and the preview matches the render. New '⧉ style from captions' link on each title card: one click copies the current caption look (font, colour, case, outline, shadow, plate, line spacing) into that title, then you tweak it. Fix: titles now show in the 'exact' preview too (they were only in the final render), including when a title is on screen but no caption is. Titles got FULL styling to match captions — a '⚙ More styling' block per title with case, alignment, line spacing, text width, outline colour, shadow (on/off, X/Y, blur, colour) and plate colour/alpha/padding/radius. Fix: PNG/.mov overlays now appear and disappear on their in/out in the PREVIEW as well (the render already did; the preview kept them on screen for the whole clip). Titles (was 'Headline') are now a full system: add as MANY titles as you need, each with its own font (any font from fonts/), size, colour, vertical position, outline, optional plate and its own show-from/show-to timing — all baked into the render. Because a title stays text, it's localizable: the LOC tab now has a 'Переклад тайтлів' grid (titles × languages) where you type each language's copy, and every language version renders with its own text. Fonts: you can now keep a family in its own folder (fonts/Poppins/Poppins-SemiBold.ttf) — subfolders are scanned too, and the font picker groups weights under the family name (Regular · Medium · SemiBold · Bold…) instead of a flat wall of filenames. Presets saved before a font was moved into a folder keep working. Animation: it's now clearly marked that only Typewriter survives the render — Pop and Rise are preview-only and show a warning when picked, so nobody ships expecting them. New: 'Text swaps' tablets in Smart captions — add your own transcript swaps (percent → %, workouts → wo) with ＋/✕, no JSON editing; they apply to both Whisper and Scribe. New: 'Time spent (all sessions)' in Settings — accumulated per-operation totals for today / 7 days / all time, with medians, the assembly cache hit rate and an estimate of the encoding time the cache avoided. New: the clip cache now prunes itself (entries unused for 30 days, and a 20 GB budget), so it can't grow forever; the manual Clear cache button stays. Earlier in this build: preview now matches the render exactly (single layout engine), assemble is ~8x faster (a finished body is normalized once and cached, then joined by stream copy), localizable text headlines, per-phrase styles, second word shadow, scrim fade, caption drag on the preview, Safe zones, transcript number/unit clean-up, the Assemble time board, and 'Hold last caption to end'.
